articles.title: Scientists recreate a bizarre quantum effect that stops a particle cold
articles.summary: Oxford physicists have recreated a bizarre quantum effect in which a particle responds to a magnetic field without ever traveling through it. Using a hybrid quantum computer, they demonstrated how introducing a simulated magnetic flux could completely halt a particle's movement through quantum interference. The experiment brings a decades-old prediction into a new setting where matter and quantum fields influence one another.

articles.title: This new qubit could be 100 times less error-prone in superfluid quantum computer breakthrough
articles.summary: A proposed qubit made with superfluid helium could cut quantum computing error rates by around 100 times by shielding quantum information from common forms of electromagnetic noise. If experiments confirm the predictions, the technology could eventually work alongside today’s superconducting qubits or serve as a new kind of quantum memory.

articles.title: Quantum computing’s “dark horse” just proved it can go universal
articles.summary: Researchers have shown that exotic quantum particles called non-Abelian anyons can perform the full range of operations needed for universal quantum computing. Using 54 qubits on Quantinuum’s H2 processor, they combined braiding and fusion to unlock capabilities that braiding alone could not provide.

articles.title: Scientists just made quantum computer operations 1,000 times faster
articles.summary: Researchers have found a way to perform certain quantum operations more than 1,000 times faster, cutting thousands of repeated control cycles down to just one. The advance could reduce errors and bring reliable, fault-tolerant quantum computers closer to reality.

articles.title: Former Plaud exec raises $26M for AI app that listens to you in the background
articles.summary: One of the core promises of AI is that the more it knows about a person, the better it will be able to assist them with tasks and make appropriate suggestions, which, if you'll believe the tech companies, requires apps and devices to listen, watch, or record users' activity all the time and gather all possible context.

articles.title: Will the HomeView be Apple’s first smart home success?
articles.summary: Over the past couple of years, we’ve seen multiple reports that Apple was working on a new smart home product, but now it seems the product has a name and a launch date.

articles.summary: On Equity, we debate the impact of data center moratoriums and whether the AI industry has a communication problem.

articles.title: Microsoft bets on homegrown AI chip to challenge Nvidia
articles.summary: Microsoft said Monday it will roll out its in-house Maia artificial intelligence chips on a massive scale starting in 2027, making them the main hardware for running AI across its products—a move that could reduce its reliance on Nvidia.

articles.title: Character.AI files for bankruptcy
articles.summary: Character.AI, one of the first breakout startups of the generative AI boom, has filed for bankruptcy and is selling some of its assets to Disney. The company, which builds various online bots for users to chat or roleplay with, has faced mounting scrutiny and lawsuits over the safety of its chatbots, but has continued releasing […]

articles.title: Silicon Valley is falling in line with Trump’s attempt to rename AI

While most of the broader population is sticking with AI, some of Silicon Valley's most powerful are falling in line and trying to give Trump the great AI rebrand he […]

articles.title: Learning to use local AI is exciting, overwhelming, and frustrating
articles.summary: I'm embarking on a journey I've so far been hesitant to go on: actually using AI on the regular. Giving my most personal data to cloud services has been a major hold up for me, but it's increasingly possible to run powerful models locally to see what they're capable of. Is this tech so useful […]

articles.title: Satya Nadella says we should assume all AI models are ‘compromised’
articles.summary: In a lengthy post on X, Microsoft's CEO laid out his views on the dangers posed by highly advanced AI models and how to confront those risks. Nadella says we can no longer accept a world where AI is treated as a "set of nested black boxes" whose advice and actions we simply accept or […]

articles.title: DistroKid has been quietly taking down songs in response to UMG lawsuit
articles.summary: Artists are taking to social media to complain that DistroKid has unceremoniously removed their work without notice. Now DistroKid has confirmed to The Verge that the takedowns are a direct response to claims made by UMG. The label filed a lawsuit in September claiming that DistroKid has created an "AI-slop pipeline." Artists are saying that […]

articles.title: Physicists discover “astonishing” property of light that defies expectations
articles.summary: Scientists have uncovered a surprising hidden ability of light that allows it to develop spinning, twisting behavior as it travels through empty space, without special lenses, mirrors, or materials. Researchers discovered that light’s internal geometry can naturally produce left- and right-handed patterns, challenging long-standing assumptions about how light behaves. By carefully arranging a beam’s structure, scientists can control where and how these spinning patterns emerge, unlocking a new way to manipulate light.

articles.title: This light-powered AI can spot deepfakes with nearly 98% accuracy
articles.summary: UCLA researchers built an AI system that uses light to analyze more than a dozen videos simultaneously, detecting deepfakes with nearly 98% accuracy. Its speed, low energy demands, and resistance to attacks could make it a powerful tool for screening the growing flood of AI-generated video.

articles.title: MIT’s tiny flying robot gets 450% faster with AI
articles.summary: A new AI control system lets MIT’s tiny flying robot move with insect-like agility, boosting its speed by about 450 percent and allowing it to pull off 10 somersaults in 11 seconds. The technology could eventually enable miniature robots to search earthquake rubble and navigate dangerous spaces that conventional drones cannot reach.

articles.title: The shape behind the Einstein problem just revealed strange new physics
articles.summary: A mathematical shape famous for covering a surface without ever repeating has revealed an unexpected ability to twist light into unusual chiral patterns. The discovery could lead to new ways of controlling light, polarization, and advanced optical devices.

articles.title: AI uncovers hidden Ozempic side effects across 400,000 Reddit posts
articles.summary: AI analysis of 400,000 Reddit posts found that users of drugs such as Ozempic, Wegovy, Mounjaro, and Zepbound reported unexpected symptoms including menstrual changes, chills, hot flashes, and fatigue. Researchers cannot say the medications caused these problems, but the patterns may reveal overlooked signals worth studying.

articles.title: Tiny nanolaser could cut computer energy use in half
articles.summary: Scientists have created an ultra-small nanolaser that could eventually allow microchips to transmit information with light instead of electricity, potentially making computers faster while cutting energy use roughly in half. Thousands of the lasers could fit on a single chip, opening possibilities for more efficient data centers, smartphones, and advanced medical sensors.

articles.title: Fortnite maker Epic Games makes 'huge pivot' with AI, CEO says
articles.summary: Fortnite maker Epic Games is making a "huge pivot" toward using artificial intelligence (AI) to boost video game development, CEO Tim Sweeney said on Monday.

articles.title: Will AI be good or bad for the climate? Here's what the latest evidence on energy use suggests
articles.summary: Is AI a climate change villain whose insatiable hunger for electricity will roast the planet? Or will it help predict where the next climate disaster will strike and what to do about it?

articles.title: AI framework offers new approach to teaching engineers ethical decision-making
articles.summary: Research published in the International Journal of Continuing Engineering Education and Life-Long Learning suggests that artificial intelligence is increasingly moving beyond technical automation to train engineers in ethical decision-making. The work suggests this could address a critical gap in the Industry 4.0 era.

articles.title: Smarter cities need more than smart algorithms. They need trust
articles.summary: We've never had a better understanding of how cities move, but turning that knowledge into smoother, cleaner and more equitable trips remains a challenge. The main obstacle to sustainable mobility may not be technological, but rather political and organizational.

articles.title: Just add water: New binder simplifies battery manufacturing and recycling without sacrificing performance
articles.summary: A new battery binder—the glue that holds together a battery's internal parts—could make lithium-ion batteries more environmentally friendly and easier to recycle without sacrificing performance.

articles.title: UK retains early access to test latest US AI models
articles.summary: Britain will retain early access to the latest artificial intelligence models for safety testing, the country's AI minister confirmed Monday, following reports that the White House had restricted the U.K.'s access.

articles.title: Coordinated software tools could cut AI training energy use by up to 50%
articles.summary: Around half of the energy used to train AI can be saved without affecting speed or performance, using software developed at the University of Michigan Engineering. Now, U-M researchers are working with NVIDIA to integrate their new approach into Megatron-LM, NVIDIA's open-source platform for training AI.

articles.title: From 'hands-free' to 'eyes-off': How General Motors is simulating its way to autonomous driving
articles.summary: At the General Motors Global Technical Center in Warren, Michigan, in suburban Detroit, hundreds of volunteer, real-world drivers have hopped inside a Cadillac Lyriq electric vehicle or other popular GM models and experienced all sorts of things while in the car: regular roadway driving, driving up and down hills, construction, rain, nearby traffic and other scenarios.
